correctness.rationale: The intrinsic common-center predicate places X in the cross-polytope boundary on ten antipodal pairs; the triangle inequality excludes a complementary pair from any simplex and hence excludes every setwise fixed simplex. Independently enumerated all nonempty partial choices from the ten pairs, filtered by distances to the twenty genuine centers, and checked the full two-skeleton and the six disjoint representative triple orbits with witnesses. The full two-skeleton of S^9 is simply connected, and higher cells do not affect pi1. The free double cover therefore gives pi1(Y) and integral H1(Y) both C2. For rational homology I independently oriented faces by their pair order (preserved by complement), split chains into the two characters, and used exact fraction-free pivot elimination after checking both boundary-square identities integrally. The plus ranks, in degrees 1–9, are 9,81,399,1020,1215,840,360,90,10; minus ranks are 10,80,400,1020,1215,840,360,90,10. The plus homology is the geometric quotient's rational homology by transfer, with reduced ranks 6 and 15 in degrees 3 and 4 only. The minus ranks in homology are 5 and 15 in those degrees, proving the claimed traces. Because distances between distinct triples are 2,4,6, there is no intervening change of complex for closed radii in [2,4).
residual_risks: No claim or computation of integral higher homology, integral representation or full quotient homotopy type.

value.rationale: Complement is a canonical free symmetry on this central weight layer. At the cited scale the complex has two nonzero higher rational homology groups. The exact split 6+5 and 15+15 is useful to determine quotient homology and how ordinary homology is distributed between the two characters, information neither the known wedge counts nor the free-action alternating trace gives. This is a motivated finite invariant, not an asserted family theorem or a recomputation of the ordinary homology table.
residual_risks: The application is to this exact intrinsic metric layer and scale; the computation does not classify other quotients.
